newsitem.title: USA: Buckeye sees NYC line restart soon.
newsitem.headline: Buckeye sees NYC line restart soon.

text.p: Buckeye Pipeline Co said it expects to receive the go ahead to restart the New York City section of its 200,000 barrel per day oil products pipeline "at any moment," following a shut down due to a bomb scare.
"We expect to receive permission from the police to restart Buckeye's (two parallel 12-inch) lines at any moment," Buckeye spokesman Roy Haase said Wednesday.

Buckeye supplies, among other products and other locations, jet fuel to New York City's two airports, John F Kennedy International and La Guardia, but officials do not foresee any problems at the airports due to the shutdown.

"From the Port Authority's airport operations perspective, we don't foresee any problems with air transportation," said a spokesman at the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey. The Port Authority runs the two airports, as well as nearby Newark International in New Jersey.
He noted both airports store as much as one week's worth of jet fuel at each facility.
"If worse came to worse, the jet fuel could be barged (by water) to either airport," the spokesman said.
New details on efforts to remove the package from an area on Staten Island were not immediately available.

But Buckeye remained closed, and 26-inch natural gas line running parallel to the downed Buckeye section and operated by Transcontinental Gas Pipe Line (Transco) was nearly shutdown due to the bomb scare, company officials said.
Transco is a unit of Williams Cos Inc and Buckeye is owned by Buckeye Partners LP.
The downed Buckeye line supplies all sorts of refined products besides jet fuel, including gasoline and heating oil, to other parts of New York City and neighboring Long Island to the east.
Buckeye's entire network extends north and west into upstate New York, Pennsylvania and even Ohio on the eastern edges of the U.S. midcontinent.
-- Oliver Ludwig, New York Energy Desk 1 212 859 1633
